title: Give OLY-B-BND-01 a mechanism: refuse writes to any non-origin remote
summary: Add a guard so Athena's own publishing (git push, replace, delete of branches, and PR/GitHub API writes) can reach only the repository's own `origin`, never another remote such as `upstream`. Record it in docs/spec.toml as OLY-B-BND-01's mechanism and measure, with a test that fails without the guard. Goal: the spec owner (Themis) can see the boundary enforced by code and a test.

defaults_applied.how: Criteria require a new failing-without-mechanism test and cargo test, clippy and fmt to pass.
Criteria check refusal of push to a non-origin remote by running tests.
Guard sits in the shared GitRemote write methods so every publishing path is covered.
The rule is enforced by code and recorded in docs/spec.toml.
BRIEF.md asks for tagged releases and a changelog, so the change records itself in CHANGELOG.md.

assumptions: Reading: 'upstream project' means any repository other than the one Athena works in, i.e. any git remote other than `origin` and any GitHub repository other than the one parsed from `origin`. Athena's own push of job branches and PRs to `origin` is the project's own repository and is allowed.

Environment: the guard runs locally inside the Athena process (the orchestrator's own working copy and its landing/early-push code in crates/athena-core/src/gh), not in a CI job or a producer. It acts through `git` and the `gh` runner with the owner's existing credentials; the new tests use only temporary local git repositories and a fake runner, with no network and no real GitHub access. Reach: refs `refs/heads/<job branch>` on `origin` only. With no origin, `git remote get-url origin` fails and the landing/push path errors before any write (test asserts no push). With a non-GitHub origin (local path or other host), pushes go to that origin only and GitHub PR/API writes are not attempted (`origin_repository` returns None). With a GitHub origin, pushes and PR calls target only that owner/repo. A remote named anything other than `origin` (for example `upstream`) is refused for push, replace and delete_branch.

Code survey: read crates/athena-core/src/gh/remote.rs (Remote trait; GitRemote push, replace, delete_branch take a free `name`), crates/athena-core/src/gh/landing.rs (landing hard-codes remote_name = "origin", parses it with parse_remote, builds GhClient for that repository), crates/athena-core/src/gh/early.rs (early push uses origin), crates/athena-core/src/gh/client.rs (GhClient::origin_repository, HostOperation), and crates/athena-agent/src/policy.rs (check_git allow-list denies push for agents; check_gh allows only GET reads). The entry points are the Remote impl methods and landing; the new check runs before any `git push` call. No record or data file is added under crates/, so check_record_file, AnyRecord and the round-trip test are not affected. The property is measured directly by calling GitRemote::push/replace/delete_branch against a temp repo that has an `upstream` bare remote and observing that its refs do not change.

Existing code: extends crates/athena-core/src/gh/remote.rs (GitRemote) and reuses crates/athena-agent/src/policy.rs denial of agent push and write-form gh; docs/spec.toml gets the mechanism, owner and measure on the existing OLY-B-BND-01 entry.
The measure ends `status: not shown` and names the test that shows it, because no `athena status` line reports upstream writes.
Governance files (athena.toml, defaults.toml, workflows) are not needed and do not change.
The new refusal affects only publishing calls, not readings; the replay-of-readings refusal-rate rule does not apply (expected 0% of newly refused readings).

acceptance_criteria.text: docs/spec.toml entry OLY-B-BND-01 has `mechanism` naming crates/athena-core/src/gh/remote.rs (the guard) instead of "none", keeps owner Themis, and its `measure` ends with `status: not shown` plus the name of the test that shows it (check with git diff docs/spec.toml).
The mechanism path named in the spec exists: Grep finds the guard function and its use in GitRemote push, replace and delete_branch in crates/athena-core/src/gh/remote.rs.

Run `cargo test -p athena-core` : a new test creates a temp repo with `origin` and `upstream` bare remotes, calls GitRemote push/replace/delete_branch with name `upstream`, and asserts an error and that the upstream refs are unchanged; the same test pushes to `origin` and succeeds.

Run `cargo test -p athena-core`: tests cover the three origin cases: no origin (landing/push errors, no write), a local-path origin (no GitHub call made by the fake runner), and a GitHub-style https origin (writes target only the parsed owner/repo).
The new test fails when the guard call is removed from GitRemote::push (the verifier can check the diff shows the test asserting on the refusal and not only on wiring).
`cargo fmt --check`, `cargo clippy --all-targets` and `cargo test` all pass.
Only docs/spec.toml and files under crates/ change; CHANGELOG.md, athena.toml and defaults.toml are untouched.

out_of_scope: Changing how agents' git/gh commands are policed in crates/athena-agent/src/policy.rs beyond what already exists.
Blocking Athena's own pushes and PRs to the project's `origin`.
Adding an `athena status` line for upstream writes.
hard_reason: Adds a rule that refuses publishing (a guard in the push and landing path), which is a gate on how work lands.
